case_name: Noor Mohammad Mohd. Yusuf Momin v State Of Maharashtra
respondent:
State Of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

24 March 1970
Criminal Appeal No.24 of 1968. Appeal by special leave from the judgment and order dated December 13, 14, 1967 of the Bombay High Court in Criminal Appeal No. 380 of 1966
The Judgment was delivered by : I. D. Dua, J.
1. In this appeal by special leave we are only concerned with the conviction of one out of four accused persons jointly tried for the murder of one Mohd. Yahya. The appellant Noor Mohammed Mahamed Yusef Momin, accused no. 4, in the trial court was jointly tried with three
facts: The appellant Noor Mohammed Mahamed Yusef Momin was jointly tried with three others for the murder of one Mohd. Yahya.
The trial court convicted Mohd. Taki Haji Hussein Momin, accused no. 1 under s. 302, I.P.C. and sentenced him to imprisonment for life.
All four accused persons were residents of the same place and the deceased Mohd. Yahya was a close neighbour of the appellant.

The prosecution alleged that there were constant disputes between the appellant and the deceased over the right of passage and the right to tap water, and it is not disputed that both sides had made reports and counter-reports with the police against each other.
issues: Whether the accused persons jointly tried for the murder of one Mohd. Yahya were guilty of the offence under s. 302 read with s. 34, I.P.C.
Whether the appellant was guilty of an offence under s. 302 read with s. 109, I.P.C.
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution alleged that there was a conspiracy between the accused persons to commit the murder of Mohd. Yahya after his return from Bombay and it was in pursuance of that conspiracy that he was murdered on the night of April 17, 1965.
The appellant argued that the evidence against him was circumstantial and did not establish his guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
respondent_arguments: The respondent State argued that the evidence against the accused persons was sufficient to prove their guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
The respondent State also argued that the trial court had correctly applied the principles of law in convicting the accused persons.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the prosecution had established a prima facie case against the accused persons and that the evidence against them was sufficient to prove their guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
The Court also held that the trial court had correctly applied the principles of law in convicting the accused persons.
holding: The Court upheld the conviction of the accused persons under s. 302 read with s. 34, I.P.C. and sentenced them to imprisonment for life.
The Court also upheld the conviction of the appellant under s. 302 read with s. 109, I.P.C.
